THE MEN’S EDIT | HWANG IN-YOUP MAKES AIRPORT STYLE LOOK EASY

Airport dressing does not have to mean choosing between comfort and looking put together.

Hwang In-youp makes a convincing case for both.

The South Korean actor departed Incheon for Singapore in Prada, ahead of the fashion house’s upcoming event at its newly transformed Paragon boutique.

The look is deceptively simple: a navy knit polo layered over white, relaxed beige Old Denim five-pocket jeans, white Speedrock sneakers and an oversized black Prada Buckle bag.

Nothing is particularly complicated.

And that is precisely why it works.

The navy and beige palette keeps the outfit polished without feeling formal. The longer white layer appearing underneath the polo breaks up the darker top and makes the styling feel less rigid, while the relaxed trousers give the silhouette the ease a travel look actually needs.

Then there is the bag.

Prada’s Buckle design brings structure to an otherwise very soft outfit, while its oversized proportions make sense in a travel setting. Prada describes the style as balancing functionality with a clean, architectural silhouette, while the Speedrock sneaker is designed around lightweight, flexible construction.

It is a useful reminder that good airport style is often less about adding more pieces and more about getting the proportions right.

Comfortable trousers.
A polished knit.
Practical footwear.
And a bag substantial enough to actually travel with.

Outfit ideas for bigger guys, and what I actually bought to build them.

Three outfits from one haul, all built on the same rule. If you carry weight through the middle, a slim trouser pulls tight at the thigh and tapers to nothing at the ankle, so your top half looks heavier by comparison. A wide leg holds a straight line from hip to floor. Same body, better proportion.

Look one, butter yellow linen shirt untucked over cream wide leg trousers with black penny loafers. Two shades of the same warm tone, so nothing cuts you at the waist.

Look two, black leather jacket over pleated wide leg trousers and Tabi oxfords. A cropped jacket sits at the narrowest point of your torso and lets the trouser take over. That contrast is what does the work, not the black.

Look three, linen parka over cream linen trousers with white trainers. The parka has structure through the shoulder, which is the easiest way to balance a wider middle without wearing something tight.

The thing all three share is a heavier shoe. Loafers, oxfords, chunky trainers. A wide trouser over a thin sole looks unfinished every time.

Friday Travel FAQ ✈️

Can I bring power banks in checked baggage?

No. Power banks should go in your carry-on bag, not your checked luggage.

Power banks are considered spare lithium batteries, and airline safety rules require them to be carried in the cabin where they can be monitored.

So before you check in your luggage, make sure your power bank, portable charger, and spare batteries are with you in your hand-carry bag.

A few reminders:

✅ Keep power banks in your carry-on
✅ Protect them from damage
✅ Do not pack loose spare batteries in checked luggage
✅ Check your airline’s rules, especially for larger-capacity power banks

Travel tip: If your carry-on bag gets checked at the gate, remove your power bank first and keep it with you.

Save this before your next flight.

Source: TSA, FAA, and IATA
